leadIn: By the end of this lesson, learners will be able to:
objectives: Apply React Router's Route component to define parent routes that serve as layout containers
Use the Outlet component to render nested child routes within parent route layouts
Implement a ProtectedRoute component to control access to routes based on authentication state
Execute conditional rendering within route components to display different UI based on user permissions
Utilize the useNavigate hook to programmatically redirect users when authentication checks fail
Construct nested route structures with multiple levels of parent-child relationships
Define route parameters within nested routes to access dynamic segments at different levels
Handle authentication state in a React context or state management solution to share across protected routes
Apply TypeScript interfaces to type-check route parameters and authentication props
Implement route configuration patterns that separate public routes from protected route hierarchies
Use React Router's index routes to define default content for nested route paths
Modify existing route structures to add new nested routes without breaking existing navigation
